title: Alternating bit protocol, with its unmarked-acknowledgement variant (par)
source: Own generalized model (one global transit window [L, U], storage sd), not a transliteration. Protocol idea: K. A. Bartlett, R. A. Scantlebury, P. T. Wilkinson, 'A Note on Reliable Full-Duplex Transmission over Half-Duplex Links', CACM 12(5):260-261, 1969 (the later one-way form with a resend timer is modelled). The par variant and its too-short-wait failure: D. Bosnacki and D. Dams, FORTE/PSTV 1998, pp. 423-439 (rule: the wait 'should be longer than the sum of the delays through the channels and the message processing time by the receiver'). Timed benchmark form of the protocol: the AlternatingBit model of Bonneland, Jensen, Larsen, Muniz, Srba, CAV 2018. The transliteration of the Bosnacki-Dams listing is the separate example par_timed.
property: Two assertions of the receiver. P1 (every delivery, line 602): the delivered payload is the next expected one, so nothing is delivered twice and nothing is skipped in the middle. P2 (on Done{completed: true}, line 629): when the sender believes all K messages were acknowledged, the receiver has delivered all K (no silent gap at the tail).
citable_note: The 2026-09-18 audit rated it citable with one claim withdrawn (equal cost at U = 3, 30, 300 against DT-Spin's state growth is not a timed-against-baseline result; the source header withdraws it too). The current source still meets the audit's conditions: the program is identical in both modes and the vacuity warnings are in place. Caveats: an own model, not the published listing (cite par_timed for that); the par boundary is measured on a finite set of cells, not proved, and its sd term is not exercised by the campaign (sd = 0 in every cell); holds are holds for the bounds K and R; the audit's execution counts (54 against 29) predate universal loss.
config_timed: apply_parallel(Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_progress_report(usize::MAX)) (alternating_bit_timed.rs:659-660), then .with_timed(L, U, sd) (line 666): every send in both directions has a transit time in [L, U], a message stays readable for sd after it arrives. W is the wait of the sender's receive (Finite(W), lines 537-540), dR an exact sleep of the receiver after it delivers a new frame (line 609). Every send may be dropped, without a budget (Init and Done included). Consistency model: the default, FIFO (lib.rs:355). Scheduling policy: the default, LTR (lib.rs:356). --keep-going adds with_keep_going_after_error(true) (lines 661-663): passed by the par-variant cells only; the abp-variant cells run without it. Exploration is sequential (apply_parallel, lines 647-654, default none) except in the two edge rungs, which pass --parallel shared (with_parallel(true), line 650): the shared worker pool, one worker per CPU the process is pinned to (num_cpus::get(), exec_pool.rs:379-385), 8 in the campaign.
config_baseline: The same builder without with_timed (line 665): with_all_sends_lossy (every send may be dropped, without a budget), FIFO, LTR, same keep-going option, sequential. The timed receive and the sleep run with their timing ignored, so W, U, L, sd and dR have no effect: baseline counts depend only on the variant, K and R.
program_differs_between_modes: no: sender and receiver take only the parameters; the processing sleep is unconditional (a no-op without a clock); the mode only selects the Config (lines 664-667)
failing_tasks: Only the receiver asserts (P1 at line 602, P2 at line 629). It is the first thread main spawns, so every violating execution of a keep-going run prints the line task-1 (checked in a local run of the par variant). In a run without --keep-going the first violation aborts with exit code 101; no abp-variant cell does.

counters.meaning: executions in which P1 failed (a wrong or duplicate delivery); raised once, immediately before the failing assertion, which ends the execution
executions in which P2 failed (the sender completed, the receiver misses a message at the tail). p1_fails + p2_fails equals the violating executions in every v9 run (74 of 74)
times the abp sender discarded an acknowledgement with the wrong bit: evidence that the premature-timeout path was explored. Read as zero or nonzero; always 0 for the par variant

param_columns.meaning: abp: acknowledgements repeat the frame's bit and the sender ignores a wrong one; par: acknowledgements carry no bit, any acknowledgement counts (--variant)
retransmissions per message before the sender gives up (--retries)
transit lower bound, L = round(l-ratio * U); timed side only
transit upper bound (--u, default 1); timed side only
storage lifetime: how long a message stays readable after it arrives, sd = round(sd-ratio * U); 0 in every cell
receiver's processing time after it delivers a new frame, dR = round(proc-ratio * U)
sender's timeout: how long it waits for an acknowledgement before it sends the frame again, W = round(w-ratio * U)
derived: smallest W of the violation window of the par variant, the smallest integer W >= 1 with (R + 1) W >= 2L + dR

derived: largest W of the violation window, 2U + sd + dR (the upper edge; the tie violates). The par variant violates on the timed side iff W_lo <= W <= W_hi; for the abp variant the same window is where the premature-timeout path is feasible (stale above 0)

boundary_law: par variant, timed side: a violation exists iff W <= 2U + sd + dR (upper edge; the tie violates) and 2L + dR <= (R + 1) W (lower edge). Above the upper edge a timeout can no longer be followed by a read of the acknowledgement it gave up on; below the lower edge no acknowledgement can return before the sender gives up on the first message, so nothing completes (0 violations, P2 never evaluated). The abp variant holds at every W; for it the window only says where the timed side still explores the premature-timeout path. Origin: measured with this binary (source header, 'Expected verdicts', re-measured 2026-09-30 with every send lossy, lines 318-349) and coded in its vacuity check (lines 764-770); not proved. At L = U and sd = 0 the upper edge is Bosnacki and Dams' To > dK + dL + dR. How well it is checked in v9: all 7 par-variant timed cells agree (2 one tick above the upper edge at U = 1, 2 ties, 1 one tick above the upper edge on the DT-Spin row, 1 smallest wait inside, 1 below the lower edge), at sd = 0 only.

regimes.name: abp variant, wait above the premature window (default setting)
regimes.params: L=0, U=1, sd=0, dR=0, W=3; variant abp
regimes.rule: W = 3 > 2U + sd + dR = 2: on the timed side no timeout can be followed by a read of the acknowledgement it gave up on. This variant has no violating side: acknowledgements carry the bit, so the protocol is correct at every W on order-preserving channels. Control: the clock changes the cost, not the verdict. All size ladders (messages K, retries R) run here.
regimes.expect_timed: 0 violations (stale = 0: the premature-timeout path is infeasible)
regimes.expect_baseline: 0 violations (stale above 0: without a clock the stale acknowledgement is explored and discarded)

regimes.name: par variant, wait one tick above the upper edge (default setting)
regimes.params: L=0, U=1, sd=0, dR=0, W=3; variant par
regimes.rule: W = 3 > 2U + sd + dR = 2: above the upper edge of the violation window, so the acknowledgement mix-up cannot happen in real time.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations (p1_fails and p2_fails above 0): without a clock the sender can time out early at every W and take the second acknowledgement of one message for the acknowledgement of the next

regimes.name: abp variant, wait on the upper edge of the premature window
regimes.params: L=0, U=1, sd=0, dR=0, W=2; variant abp
regimes.rule: W = 2 = 2U + sd + dR: a premature timeout followed by a read of the late acknowledgement is feasible; the abp sender discards that acknowledgement (wrong bit). Still no violation: control.
regimes.expect_timed: 0 violations (stale above 0: the premature-timeout path is explored)
regimes.expect_baseline: 0 violations, the same counts as in A-ctrl (the baseline ignores W)

regimes.name: par variant, wait on the upper edge (tie)
regimes.params: L=0, U=1, sd=0, dR=0, W=2; variant par
regimes.rule: W = 2 = 2U + sd + dR: exactly on the upper edge; the lower-edge condition 2L + dR = 0 <= (R + 1) W holds. The tool puts the tie on the violating side (a timeout and an arrival at the same instant may be ordered either way).
regimes.expect_baseline: violations, the same counts as in A-safe: the baseline ignores W, U, L, sd and dR (no baseline job of its own)

regimes.name: abp variant, wait inside the premature window
regimes.params: L=0, U=1, sd=0, dR=0, W=1; variant abp
regimes.rule: W = 1 < 2U + sd + dR = 2: premature timeouts are feasible at every send. Still no violation: control. The timed side explores 0.71 of the baseline's executions here (v8, K=4).
regimes.expect_baseline: 0 violations, the same counts as in A-ctrl (the baseline ignores W)

regimes.name: par variant, DT-Spin row, wait on the upper edge (tie)
regimes.params: L=3, U=3, sd=0, dR=1, W=7; variant par
regimes.rule: W = 7 = 2U + sd + dR, which at L = U = 3 is Bosnacki and Dams' dK + dL + dR with their constants (3, 3, 1): exactly on the upper edge. The lower-edge condition 2L + dR = 7 <= (R + 1) W = 21 holds. The tool puts the tie on the violating side, as the published rule To > dK + dL + dR does.
regimes.expect_baseline: violations, the same counts as in A-safe: the baseline ignores W, U, L, sd and dR (no baseline job of its own)

regimes.name: par variant, DT-Spin row, first wait above the upper edge
regimes.params: L=3, U=3, sd=0, dR=1, W=8; variant par
regimes.rule: W = 8 = 2U + sd + dR + 1: the smallest wait the published rule To > dK + dL + dR = 7 allows.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations (p1_fails and p2_fails above 0): without a clock the sender can time out early at every W and take the second acknowledgement of one message for the acknowledgement of the next

regimes.name: par variant, DT-Spin row, smallest wait inside the window
regimes.params: L=3, U=3, sd=0, dR=1, W=3; variant par
regimes.rule: W = 3 <= 2U + sd + dR = 7 and 2L + dR = 7 <= (R + 1) W = 9 at R = 2: inside the violation window. W = 3 is the smallest integer wait that meets the lower-edge condition (not a tie: 9 > 7).
regimes.expect_baseline: violations, the same counts as in A-safe: the baseline ignores W, U, L, sd and dR (no baseline job of its own)

regimes.name: par variant, DT-Spin row, wait below the lower edge: nothing completes
regimes.params: L=3, U=3, sd=0, dR=1, W=2; variant par
regimes.rule: (R + 1) W = 6 < 2L + dR = 7 at R = 2: no acknowledgement can come back before the sender gives up on the first message, so no execution completes. 0 violations, but P2 is never evaluated (end_checks = 0, the binary prints a WARNING): a partial hold, to be read as 'no completion'.
regimes.expect_timed: 0 violations (no execution completes: end_checks = 0, P1 checked only)
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations, the same counts as in A-safe: the baseline ignores W (no baseline job of its own)

glossary.meaning: the alternating bit protocol proper: every acknowledgement repeats the bit of the frame it answers and the sender ignores an acknowledgement with the wrong bit. Correct at every timeout on channels that keep the order

the same protocol with unmarked acknowledgements (any acknowledgement counts): a wait shorter than the round trip lets the sender take the second acknowledgement of one message for the acknowledgement of the next, which is then never resent
a data message: the alternating bit plus the payload (0 to K-1)
the receiver's reply to every frame, new or duplicate
the sender's wait for an acknowledgement, in ticks, counted from the (re)send
bounds of the transit time of every message, in ticks, in both directions
storage lifetime in ticks: a message not read within sd of its arrival expires
the receiver's processing time, an exact sleep after a new frame is delivered and before its acknowledgement is sent
the waits W for which the par variant violates on the timed side: W_lo <= W <= W_hi
2U + sd + dR: the largest wait at which a timeout can still be followed by a read of the acknowledgement it gave up on
the smallest wait with (R + 1) W >= 2L + dR: below it the sender gives up on the first message before any acknowledgement can return
W = W_hi: the timeout and the latest possible arrival fall on the same instant; both orders are possible and the cell violates
the sender resends although the acknowledgement is still on its way. Harmless for abp (the late acknowledgement has the wrong bit and is discarded, counted in stale), fatal for par
the constants of Bosnacki and Dams' Table 2, first row, in this model's parameters: L = U = 3 (dK = dL = 3), dR = 1; flags --u 3 --l-ratio 1 --proc-ratio 0.333
an exit-0 run in which no execution reaches Done{completed: true} (end_checks = 0): P2 was never evaluated, so the run is not a hold of P2
executions in which P1 or P2 failed; their sum is the number of violating executions
event counter: acknowledgements with the wrong bit that the abp sender discarded
summary counter (events): the sender accepted an acknowledgement that answers an older frame; 0 in every abp-variant run and on the safe side of the par variant

glossary.term: delivered, dups, timeouts, completed, gave_up, end_checks
glossary.meaning: summary counters (events over all explored executions, read as zero or nonzero): frames handed to the user, old copies acknowledged again, retransmissions, senders that got all K acknowledgements, senders that gave up after R retransmissions, evaluations of P2. Their values on the timed side changed between v8 and v9 although the execution counts did not, so never compare them across campaigns
harness messages: main's bootstrap and the sender's end marker. Like every send they may be dropped; the waiting thread then blocks (a blocked execution, not a violation)

on the timed side a stored message that is not read within sd is gone. With dR above 0 a frame can expire while the receiver processes an earlier one: a loss the baseline does not have (the binary prints a NOTE on the DT-Spin rows)

notes: Regime letters are new in v9 (v8 had none for ABP). One letter = one complete timing setting: A (L=0, U=1, sd=0, dR=0, W=3: the default, all size ladders), B (same network, W=2), C (same network, W=1), D (DT-Spin row at the upper edge: W=7 and W=8), E (DT-Spin row at the lower edge: W=3 and W=2). On A and B the variant decides the suffix: abp is a control (no violating side exists), par is safe or on the edge.

Boundary cells checked against the law (par, timed: violation iff W <= 2U + sd + dR and 2L + dR <= (R + 1) W). U=1 (window W = 1 to 2): abp premature W=2 (on the upper edge) and W=1 (inside): no violation, stale above 0, as predicted for abp; par edge W=2 (tie): violation, found (97964). DT-Spin row at R=2 (window W = 3 to 7): W=7 (tie): violation, found (7462); W=8: none, found 0 with P2 evaluated; W=3 (smallest inside): violation, found (37730); W=2 (below, 6 < 7): no completion, found (execs=27, end_checks=0). No mismatch. Still unmeasured in v9 on the timed side: abp premature K=4 W=1 and K=5 W=2 (v8: holds with stale above 0).

Many cells exist on the timed side only. (1) par K=5 R=2: one baseline computation serves all six cells, because the baseline ignores W, U, L and dR. It has two jobs, abp-004 (U=1, W=3) and abp-033 (DT-Spin row, W=8); v8 measured them bit-identical (execs=44528549 blocked=45323189 p1_fails=794622 p2_fails=2552172); neither has a v9 result yet. The rows B-edge, D-edge, E-viol and E-safe have no baseline side of their own in the plan. (2) abp ladders above K=6 (R=2) and above R=7 (K=2) have no baseline job: the baseline did not finish K=6 or R=7 in v8.

The baseline ignores W: v9 measures the abp baseline at K=4 R=2 three times (W = 3, 2, 1) with identical counts (execs=4503679 blocked=4503697) and at K=5 R=2 twice (W = 3, 2: execs=188828658 blocked=188828676). Those baseline rows are replicates of one computation.

kind = first-violation on the abp-variant cells only records that they run without --keep-going. Every finished one ended with exit code 0, so each explored its whole space and its counts are exhaustive. The par-variant cells run with --keep-going: a violating run exits with code 0 and the verdict is the count (plus the VIOLATION line), never the exit code. A local run of a small par tie cell without --keep-going (K=2, R=1, U=1, W=2, binary of 30 September) aborts with exit code 101 and a certified witness.

No single violation counter: violating executions = p1_fails + p2_fails (two different assertions). The sum equals the tool's count in all 74 finished v9 runs (12 of them with violations), so violation_counter is null and the two counters are listed instead. All runs are sequential, so the pool effect seen on the PAR sheet (a few violation lines lost) cannot occur here.

Disagreement between memory notes and source, the source wins. (1) The 2026-09-16 case-study note gives the upper edge as 2U + 2sd + dR; the source (re-measured 2026-09-30) says 2U + sd + dR: one sd went away with the timeout-miss rule, under which a timeout may not pass over a readable acknowledgement. The binary still prints '(2U+2sd+dR=..)' in its summary line, for reference only (lines 505-510). With sd = 0 in every campaign cell the two expressions coincide, so v9 cannot tell them apart and says nothing about the sd term. (2) The same note records that Sahar asked for the example to use unordered (bag) channels and calls the header's bullet 'Order-preserving channels instead of TAPAAL's unordered media' out of date. The committed source sets no consistency model, so every cell runs on FIFO channels, and the bullet is still in the header (lines 169-171). (3) The audit's execution counts for the default cell (54 against 29) predate universal loss; the header now gives 122 + 132 against 34 + 44.

Event counters (delivered, dups, timeouts, stale, confused, completed, gave_up) changed on the timed side between v8 and v9 while execs, blocked, p1_fails and p2_fails are identical in all 28 jobs finished in both campaigns (example: stale at abp premature K=4 W=2 was 604703 in v8 and is 485108 in v9, on the same 263236 + 263254 executions); on the baseline side no counter changed. Use them as zero or nonzero evidence only. Where a v9 result is missing, this file quotes v8 execution counts but never a v8 event count.

Above the edge the two variants are the same computation on the timed side: at W=3 abp and par report identical counts (K=4: 8002 + 8020; K=5: 56022 + 56040), because no stale acknowledgement can ever be read.

Cost is not uniform across the regimes. A (W=3): timed explores far less (K=5 R=2: 112062 against 377657334) and is far faster (48 s against 7 h 25 min). B-ctrl (W=2): K=4, 526490 explored in 222 s against 9007376 in 582 s. C-ctrl (W=1): in v8 the timed side explored 0.71 of the baseline's executions and took 4690 s against 823 s. The premature-timeout path costs the timed side most of its advantage.

E-safe (below the lower edge) is a partial hold: 0 violations because nothing completes, P2 never evaluated. It carries the suffix safe because the clock rules the violation out, but it must not be reported as a hold of both properties. Its counts (execs=27, blocked=45) do not depend on K.

Timed execution counts follow closed forms in A-ctrl: execs = (10 * 7^K - 4) / 3 at R=2 (blocked = execs + 18) and execs = 3n^2 - 4n + 2 with n = 2^(R+1) at K=2 (blocked = execs + 2n + 2). They fit all 13 measured sizes (K = 3 to 8, R = 4 to 10) and give the plan's predictions for the edge rungs: K=9, 134512022 execs; R=11, 50315266 execs. Observed regularities, not derived formulas.

The two edge rungs (abp-e01, K=9; abp-e02, R=11) are the only cells of this example that use the shared worker pool (8 cores); the rest of both ladders is sequential. This file has no pool-size column so that the rungs stay attached to their ladders; their wall times must not be put on the same axis as the sequential rungs. The parameters of the edge flags were checked with a local run of the same flags at K=2, R=1: L=0 U=1 sd=0 W=3 dR=0.

Ratio flags resolve as round(ratio * U): all 74 v9 summary lines carry the values this file lists (checked by script). The cells without a v9 row were checked against their v8 summary line (abp-004, abp-006, abp-013, abp-020, abp-026, abp-028, abp-033) or, for the two ceiling baselines and the two edge rungs, against cells with the same timing flags.
